meta.title: Political methodology knowledge network, c. 1935-2026
meta.description: Key works and debates in political methodology: the potential-outcomes framework and causal mechanisms, regression and matching, difference-in-differences, fixed effects and synthetic control, natural experiments, instrumental variables and regression discontinuity, field experiments, survey experiments, conjoint and list experiments, ideal-point scaling, measurement and latent variables, text as data, machine learning and heterogeneous effects, large language models for annotation and measurement, Bayesian and multilevel models, time-series cross-section data, missing data, survey methodology, qualitative and multi-method research, formal models and EITM, replication and transparency, and networks and spatial interdependence. Works shared with the other maps are imported from them; others are top-cited 2006-2026 articles selected via Crossref (Political Analysis, PSRM, Sociological Methods & Research, JASA and methods articles in general political science journals) and anchoring books and classics. Direction: source (later or dependent work) -> target (earlier or anchoring work).

edge_types.builds_on: source extends or relies on target's argument or evidence
edge_types.challenges: source contests target's claim, mechanism or evidence
edge_types.qualifies: source adds a scope condition or moderating factor to target
edge_types.extends_to_new_case: source applies target's logic to a new population, period or domain
edge_types.synthesizes: source integrates target with other work
edge_types.mechanism_tested_by: source tests a mechanism implied by target

meta.verification: Repo works come from the user's Zotero library. Works imported from the other maps keep their verification. Crossref-selected works take title, authors, year, venue and DOI from Crossref records. Anchors are checked in Crossref separately; see each node's `verified` field. One-line claims for non-repo works are my summaries.
